claims.text: At stage-2 ProductListScreen is a ConsumerWidget with no constructor parameters besides key; its build(BuildContext, WidgetRef ref) calls ref.watch(productsProvider) and does not watch apiClientProvider itself.
apiClientProvider is a top-level final Provider<ApiClient> whose function returns ApiClient(readToken: ...); productsProvider's function calls ref.watch(apiClientProvider).fetchProducts().
main.dart line 15 is runApp(const ProviderScope(child: DonHangApp())); DonHangApp is itself a ConsumerWidget whose build watches routerProvider, which does not read apiClientProvider.
A provider declaration only describes how to create a value; the value (provider state) is stored by ProviderScope (its ProviderContainer), not in the top-level variable.

Providers are lazy: the function runs on the first read, and later reads under the same ProviderScope return the stored value without running it again until the value is thrown away (e.g. ref.invalidate); apiClientProvider always returns the identical ApiClient.

claims.text: A ConsumerWidget's build receives a WidgetRef as its second parameter; ref.watch(provider) returns the provider's value; a provider's function receives a Ref and can ref.watch other providers; ref.read also returns a provider's value.

claims.text: Stage-2 adds screens the browser can open directly from their address, such as a product's page at /products/<id>, which no earlier screen opened.
At stage-2 the ApiClient no longer keeps a token field: readToken returns the current token, which lives in another provider (authProvider).
Asking a provider for a dependency plays the role the DI container plays in DonHang.Api: the code that uses a dependency names it instead of receiving it from whoever created it.
At stage-2 the app still has one ApiClient: every reader of apiClientProvider under the app's ProviderScope gets the same object.

claims.text: At stage-1 DonHangApp created the ApiClient and passed it to ProductListScreen, which passed it to LoginScreen, which passed it to CreateOrderScreen, all through constructors.

When the app opens at /, the ApiClient is first created when ProductListScreen watches productsProvider, whose function watches apiClientProvider (opened at /products/<id>, productProvider is the first reader instead).

At stage-2 every screen that calls the API (product list, product and order detail, create order) reaches the ApiClient through providers, not constructor parameters; productsProvider's stored value carries the loaded list.
